translations.text: In my first account, Theophilus, I wrote about everything Jesus began to do and teach,
up to the day when he was taken up, after he had instructed the apostles he had chosen, through the Holy Spirit, to proclaim the gospel.
He also presented himself alive to them after his death, with many signs, appearing to them for forty days and speaking about the kingdom of God.
While eating with them, he instructed them not to leave Jerusalem, but to wait for the Father's promise, which, he said, “You heard from me.”
He said, “John baptized with water, but you will be baptized with the Holy Spirit in not many days, by Pentecost.”
So they gathered together and asked him, “Lord, will you give the kingdom to Israel at this time?”
He said to them, “It is not for you to know the times and periods that the Father has established by his own authority.
But you will receive power when the Holy Spirit comes upon you, and you will be my witnesses in Jerusalem, throughout Judea and Samaria, and to the ends of the earth.”
After he said these things, a cloud took him, and he was lifted up away from them.
While they were watching him as he went up into heaven, two men in white clothes stood beside them.
They said to them, “Men of Galilee, why are you standing looking up into heaven? This Jesus, who was taken up from you into heaven, will come in the same way you saw him going up into heaven.”
Then they returned to Jerusalem from the mountain called the Mount of Olives, which is a journey of seven stadia from Jerusalem.

When they entered, they went up to the upstairs room where they were staying: Peter, John, James, Andrew, Philip, Thomas, Bartholomew, Matthew, James son of Alphaeus, Simon the Zealot, and Judas son of James.
They all devoted themselves to prayer, together with some women, Mary the mother of Jesus, and his brothers.
In those days Peter stood up among the brothers and sisters—there was a crowd of about one hundred and twenty people there—and said:
“Brothers, this scripture had to be fulfilled, which the Holy Spirit spoke beforehand through the mouth of David about Judas, who became a guide to those who arrested Jesus.
For he had been counted among us and had received a share in this ministry.”
This man bought himself a field with the reward for his wrongdoing. He fell on his face, split open in the middle, and all his intestines spilled out.
This became known to everyone living in Jerusalem, so that in their language they called that field Akeldama, which means Field of Blood.
“For it is written in the book of Psalms, ‘Let his dwelling become deserted, and let no one live in his dwelling places,’ and, ‘Let someone else take his position as overseer.’
So it is necessary that, from among the men who accompanied us throughout the whole time when the Lord Jesus came and went among us,
beginning with John's baptism until the day he was taken up from us, one of these should become a witness with us to his resurrection.”
They put forward two men: Joses, called Barsabbas, who was also named Justus, and Matthias.
They prayed, saying, “Lord, you know everyone's heart. Show which one of these two you have chosen.”
To take the place in this ministry and apostleship that Judas abandoned to go to his own place.
They cast lots for them, and the lot fell to Matthias, and he was counted among the eleven apostles.
When the day of Pentecost came, they were all together.
Suddenly a sound came from heaven like a violently rushing wind, and it filled the whole house where they were sitting.
Divided tongues appeared to them, as if made of fire, and settled on each one of them.
They were all filled with the Holy Spirit and began speaking in other languages, as the Spirit enabled them to speak in them.
Now there were Jews living in Jerusalem, devout people from every nation under heaven.
When this sound occurred, the crowd gathered and was bewildered, because each person heard them speaking in his own language.
They were all astonished and amazed, saying, “Aren’t all these people who are speaking Galileans?
Then how do we each hear them in our own native language?
Parthians, Medes, Elamites, and those living in Mesopotamia, Judea and Cappadocia, Pontus and Asia,
Phrygia and Pamphylia, Egypt and the parts of Libya around Cyrene, and the Romans who are here,
Jews and converts to Judaism, Cretans and Arabs—we hear them speaking in languages, proclaiming the great deeds of God.”
They were all astonished and perplexed, saying to one another, “What is this?”
But others mocked them, saying, “They are full of new wine.”
Then Peter stood up with the eleven, raised his voice, and answered them: “Jewish men and everyone living in Jerusalem, let this be clear to you, and listen to my words.
These people are not drunk, as you suppose, for it is the third hour of the day.
Rather, this is what was spoken through the prophet Joel:
‘After these things,’ God says, ‘I will pour out my Spirit on all people. Your sons and your daughters will prophesy, your young men will see visions, and your old men will dream dreams.
And I will pour out my Spirit on my male servants and my female servants in those days, and they will prophesy.
I will give signs in heaven and wonders below on the earth: blood, fire, and a cloud of smoke.
The sun will turn to darkness and the moon to blood before the great and openly revealed day of the Lord comes.
And everyone who calls on the name of the Lord will be saved.’
Men of Israel, listen to my words: Jesus of Nazareth was a man whom God singled out for you through mighty deeds, signs, and wonders that God performed through him among you, as you yourselves know.
According to God’s determined plan and knowledge, you handed this man over into the hands of lawless men, crucified him, and killed him.
God raised him up, freeing him from the pains of death, because it was impossible for him to be held by it.
For David says about him, ‘I always saw the Lord before me, because he is at my right hand so that I will not be shaken.
Because of this, my heart rejoiced and my tongue was glad. My body, too, will rest in hope,
because you will not abandon my soul in the realm of the dead, nor will you allow your Holy One to see decay.
You have shown me the paths of life; you will fill me with joy in your presence.
Brothers, we may speak openly to you about the patriarch David: he died and was buried, and his tomb is still among us to this day.
Since he was a prophet and knew that God had sworn an oath to him to seat one of his descendants on his throne,
he foresaw and spoke about the resurrection of Christ: he was not abandoned in Hades, nor did his flesh experience decay.
This is Jesus, whom God raised up, and we are all witnesses to him.
So, having been exalted at God's right hand and having received from the Father the promise of the Holy Spirit, he poured out this gift that you yourselves see and hear.
For it was not David who ascended into heaven, but he himself says, ‘The Lord said to my Lord, “Sit at my right hand.”’
Until I make your enemies a footstool for your feet.
Therefore, let the whole house of Israel know with certainty that God has made him both Lord and Christ—this Jesus whom you crucified.
When they heard these things, they were deeply troubled in their hearts and said to Peter and the rest of the apostles, ‘Brothers, what should we do?’
Peter said to them, “Repent, and let each of you be baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ for the forgiveness of your sins, and you will receive the gift of the Holy Spirit.”
For the promise is for you and your children and everyone who is far away, those whom the Lord our God will call.
With many other words he testified and pleaded with them, saying, ‘Save yourselves from this crooked generation.’
Those who accepted his message were baptized, and three thousand people were added to them that day.
They continued steadfastly in the apostles' teaching, in sharing in the breaking of bread, and in prayers.
Great fear came over everyone, for many signs and wonders were taking place through the apostles.
All who had believed were together and held everything in common.
They sold their properties and possessions and distributed them to everyone according to each person's need.
Every day they continued to meet together in the temple, and they broke bread at home, eating their food with joy and sincerity of heart.
They were praising God and enjoying the favor of all the people. Every day the Lord added to their number those who were to be saved, bringing them together.
Peter and John were going up to the temple at the ninth hour, the time of prayer.
There was a man who had been lame since he was in his mother's womb. He was carried and placed at the temple gate called Beautiful, where he would beg for charity from those entering the temple.
When he saw Peter and John about to enter the temple, he begged them to give him some charity.
Peter, together with John, looked intently at him, and they said to him, ‘Look at us.’
He looked at them, expecting to receive something from them.
But Peter said to him, ‘I have neither silver nor gold, but what I have I will give you. In the name of Jesus Christ the Nazarene, walk!’
He took him by his right hand and raised him up. Immediately his feet and ankles became strong.
He jumped up, stood, and walked. He entered the temple with them, walking and jumping and praising God.
All the people saw him walking and praising God.
They recognized him as the man who used to sit and beg for alms at the Beautiful Gate of the temple. They were filled with fear and amazement at what had happened to him.
While he was holding on to Peter and John, all the people gathered around them in the portico called Solomon’s, greatly astonished.
When Peter saw this, he said to them, “People of Israel, why are you amazed at this? Why do you stare at us as though we had done this by our own power or godliness?
The God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, the God of our ancestors, has glorified his Son Jesus, whom you handed over and denied before Pilate, even though Pilate had decided to release him.
But you denied the Holy and Righteous One and asked for a murderer to be released to you.
You killed the author of life, whom God raised from the dead. We are witnesses to him.
Through faith in his name, his name has strengthened this man whom you see and know. The faith that comes through him has given this man this health in the presence of you all.
Now, my brothers, I know that you acted in ignorance, as your rulers also did.
But in this way God fulfilled what he had foretold from the beginning through the mouths of all the prophets—that his Christ would suffer these things.
So repent and turn back, so that your sins may be wiped away,
so that, when times of relief come from the presence of the Lord, he may send the one appointed for us, Christ Jesus.
He must remain in heaven until the times of the fulfillment of all the things God spoke of long ago through the mouths of his holy prophets.
Moses said to our ancestors, ‘The Lord our God will raise up for you a prophet like me from among your brothers. Listen to him in everything he tells you.
And every person who does not listen to that prophet will be destroyed from among the people.’
All the prophets, too, from Samuel onward, including those who came after him, spoke and proclaimed these days.
You are the children of the prophets and of the covenant God established with your ancestors, saying to Abraham, ‘Through your offspring all the families of the earth will be blessed.’
You were the first for whom God raised up his Son and sent him to bless you by turning each of you away from your wickedness.”
While they were speaking to the crowd, the priests, the captain of the temple guard, and the Sadducees came upon them,
deeply troubled because they were teaching the people and proclaiming the resurrection of the dead in Jesus.
They seized them and put them in custody until the next day, because evening had already come.
But many of those who heard the message believed, and their number reached five thousand men.
The next day their rulers, elders, and scribes gathered in Jerusalem.
along with Annas the high priest, Caiaphas, John, Alexander, and those who belonged to the high priests’ family.
They made them stand in their midst and asked them, “By what power or in what name did you do this?”
Then Peter, filled with the Holy Spirit, said to them, “Rulers of the people and elders,
if we are being questioned today about the healing of a weak man, and by whom he was healed,

Let it be known to all of you and to all the people of Israel that it is in the name of Jesus Christ the Nazarene, whom you crucified but whom God raised from the dead—it is through him that this man stands before you healed.
He is the stone rejected by you builders, which has become the cornerstone.
And there is salvation in no one else, for there is no other name under heaven given to human beings through which we can be saved.
When they saw the boldness of Peter and John and realized that they were ordinary men who did not know how to read and write, they were amazed. They also recognized that they had been with Jesus.
And since they also saw the man who had been healed standing with them, they could find nothing to say.
He ordered them to go outside the council, and they spoke with one another.
They said, “What are we going to do with these men? For a clear miraculous sign has taken place through them, and it is evident to everyone living in Jerusalem, and we cannot deny it.”
But so that the message does not spread further among the people, let us order them not to speak to anyone about this name from now on.
They called them and ordered them not to speak at all or to teach in the name of Jesus.
But Peter and John answered them, saying, “Judge whether it is right before God to listen to you rather than to God.
For we cannot refrain from speaking about what we have seen and heard.”
Then they threatened them and released them, finding no way to punish them because of the people, since they were all glorifying God for what had happened.
For the man on whom this sign of healing had taken place was more than forty years old.
When they were released, they went to their own people and told them what the chief priests and elders had said to them.
When they heard this, they raised their voices together to God, saying, “Lord, you are the God who made heaven and earth and the sea and everything in them.
The Holy Spirit said through the mouth of our father David, your servant, as you said: ‘Why did the nations exalt themselves, and the peoples devise futile things?
The kings of the earth took their stand, and the rulers gathered together to fight against the Lord and against his Christ.’
For truly, in this city, Herod and Pontius Pilate, together with the nations and the people of Israel, gathered against your holy Son Jesus, whom you anointed,
to do what your hand and your plan had determined beforehand would happen.
Now, Lord, look upon their anger and enable your servants to proclaim your word with complete boldness,
as you stretch out your hand for healings, and for signs and wonders to take place through the name of your holy Son Jesus.”
When they had prayed, the place where they were gathered shook. They were all filled with the Holy Spirit and proclaimed the word of God with complete boldness.
The multitude of those who believed were of one heart and one soul. No one said that any of their possessions were their own, but they held everything in common.
With great power the apostles gave their testimony to the resurrection of the Lord Jesus, and great grace was upon them all.
For no one among them was in need, because those who owned fields or houses sold them and brought the proceeds,
laying them at the apostles’ feet. Each person was given what they needed.
Now Joses, whom the apostles called Barnabas—which is translated “son of encouragement”—was a Levite, a Cypriot by birth.
He owned a field, sold it, brought the money, and laid it at the apostles’ feet.
But a man named Ananias, together with Sapphira his wife, sold a piece of land.
He kept back some of its price, with his wife also knowing about it, and brought a portion and laid it at the apostles’ feet.
But Peter said to him, “Ananias, why has Satan filled your heart so that you lie to the Holy Spirit and keep back some of the price of the land?
Was it not yours while you owned it? And after you sold it, was it not under your control? Why did you put this in your heart, to do this evil thing? You have not lied to people, but to God.”
When Ananias heard these words, he fell down and died. Great fear fell upon everyone who heard.
The young men got up, wrapped his body, carried him out, and buried him.
After three hours, his wife came in, not knowing what had happened.
Peter said to her, “Tell me, did you sell the land for this amount of money?” She said, “Yes, for that amount.”
Then Peter said to her, “Why did you agree with each other to test the Spirit of the Lord? Look, the feet of those who buried your husband are at the door, and they will carry you out.”
Immediately she fell at his feet and died. The young men came in and found her dead. They carried her out and buried her beside her husband.
Great fear came upon the whole church and everyone who heard about these things.
Many signs and wonders were taking place among the people through the hands of the apostles. They were all together in the temple, under Solomon’s colonnade.
None of the others dared to join them, but the people honored them.
More and more believers in the Lord were being added to them, a great number of men and women.
As a result, people brought the sick out into the streets and laid them on couches and beds, so that when Peter came by, his shadow might fall on one of them.
Crowds from the towns around Jerusalem also gathered, bringing the sick and those tormented by unclean spirits, and they were all healed.
Then the high priest rose up, along with everyone who was with him and the sect of the Sadducees. They were filled with jealousy.
They laid their hands on the apostles and threw them into prison.
An angel of the Lord opened the prison doors during the night, brought them out, and said to them:
“Go, stand in the temple, and proclaim to the people all the words of this life.”

When they heard this, they went into the temple early in the morning and began teaching. The high priest and those with him came and assembled the council and all the elders of the people of Israel. They sent to the prison to have them brought in.
But when the officers went, they did not find them in the prison. They returned and reported it,
saying, “We found the prison securely locked and the guards standing at the doors, but when we opened it, we found no one inside.”
When the captain of the temple guard and the chief priests heard these words, they were puzzled about them.
Then someone came and told them, “Look, the men you threw into prison are standing in the temple, teaching the people.”
Then the captain went with the officers and brought them back without force, because they were afraid that the people might stone them.
When they brought them, they made them stand before the council, and the high priest questioned them.
He said, “Did we not strictly order you not to teach in this name? Yet look, you have filled Jerusalem with your teaching, and you want to bring this man’s blood upon us.”
But Peter and the apostles answered, “We must obey God rather than human beings.
The God of our ancestors raised Jesus, whom you killed by hanging him on a tree.
God exalted him in his glory as Leader and Savior, to give Israel repentance and forgiveness of sins through him.
We are witnesses to these things, as is the Holy Spirit, whom God gave to those who obey him.”
When they heard this, they became furious and wanted to kill them.
Then a Pharisee named Gamaliel, a teacher of the law respected by all the people, stood up in the council and ordered the apostles to leave the room for a little while.
He said to the rulers and those assembled, “Men of Israel, be careful about what you intend to do to these men.
For before these days, Theudas rose up, claiming to be someone, and four hundred men followed him. But he was killed, and all who obeyed him dispersed and came to nothing.
After him, Judas the Galilean rose up in the days of the census and drew many people after him. He too was killed, and all who obeyed him were scattered.
“Now, therefore, I tell you: keep away from these men and leave them alone. For if this plan or this work comes from human beings, it will fall apart.”
But if it is from God, you will not be able to destroy it, lest you be found fighting against God.” And they were persuaded by him.
They called the apostles in, beat them, ordered them not to speak in the name of Jesus, and released them.
They left the council rejoicing that they had been considered worthy to suffer humiliation for the name.
Every day, in the temple and in their home, they never stopped teaching and proclaiming the Lord Jesus Christ.
In those days, as the number of disciples increased, a complaint arose among the Greeks against the Hebrews because their widows were being overlooked in the daily service.
The Twelve called together the whole group of disciples and said to them, “It is not right for us to leave the word of God behind and serve tables.
So, brothers, choose seven men from among you who have a good reputation and are full of the Holy Spirit and wisdom, so that we may put them in charge of this task.
But we will devote ourselves to prayer and to the ministry of the word.”

This proposal pleased the whole group. They chose Stephen, a man full of faith and the Holy Spirit, along with Philip, Prochorus, Nicanor, Timon, Parmenas, and Nicolaus, a convert to Judaism from Antioch.
They presented these men before the apostles, who prayed and laid their hands on them.
The word of God continued to spread, and the number of disciples in Jerusalem increased greatly. A large number of priests became obedient to the faith.
Stephen, full of grace and power, performed great signs and wonders among the people through the name of the Lord Jesus Christ.
Then some people from the synagogue of those called Freedmen, along with Cyrenians, Alexandrians, and people from Cilicia and Asia, rose up and argued with Stephen.
But they could not withstand the wisdom and the Spirit by which he spoke.
Then they secretly put forward men who said, “We heard him speaking blasphemous words against Moses and God.”
They stirred up the people, the elders, and the scribes. They came upon him, seized him, and brought him before the council.
And they brought forward false witnesses who said, “This man does not stop speaking against this holy place and the law.
For we heard him say that Jesus the Nazarene will destroy this place and change the customs that Moses handed down to you.”
Everyone sitting in the council looked intently at him and saw that his face was like the face of an angel.
The high priest said to him, “Are these things so?”
He answered, “My brothers and fathers, listen to me. The God of glory appeared to our father Abraham while he was in Mesopotamia, before he settled in Haran.
He said to him, ‘Leave your land and your relatives, and come to the land that I will show you.’
Then he left the land of the Chaldeans and settled in Haran. After his father died, he was moved from there to this land where you now live.
And he gave him no inheritance in it, not even enough ground to set a foot on. But he promised to give it to him as a possession, and to his descendants after him, although he had no child.
God spoke to him, saying, ‘Your descendants will live as foreigners in a land that is not theirs, and they will be enslaved and mistreated for four hundred years.
But I myself will judge the nation they will serve as slaves,’ God said, ‘and after that they will come out and worship me in this place.’
And he gave him the covenant of circumcision. So Abraham became the father of Isaac and circumcised him on the eighth day. Isaac became the father of Jacob, and Jacob of the twelve patriarchs.
The patriarchs were jealous of Joseph and sold him into Egypt. But God was with him.
He rescued him from all his troubles and gave him favor and wisdom before Pharaoh, the king of Egypt, who appointed him ruler over Egypt and his entire household.
A famine came over all Egypt and Canaan, along with great distress, and our fathers could not find food.
When Jacob heard that there was grain in Egypt, he sent our fathers there for the first time.
On the second visit, Joseph made himself known to his brothers, and Pharaoh learned about Joseph’s family.
Joseph sent for his father Jacob and all his relatives, seventy-five people in all.
Jacob went down to Egypt, and he and our fathers died.
They were brought to Shechem and laid in the tomb that Abraham had bought for a sum of money from the sons of Hamor in Shechem.
As the time drew near for the promise that God had made to Abraham, God increased the people, and they multiplied in Egypt.
Until another king arose over Egypt who did not know Joseph.
He plotted against our people and mistreated our fathers, forcing them to abandon their children so that they would not survive.
At that time Moses was born, and he was beautiful in God’s sight. He was cared for in his father’s house for three months.
When he was abandoned, Pharaoh’s daughter took him in and raised him as her own son.
Moses was educated in all the wisdom of the Egyptians, and he was powerful in his words and deeds.
When he reached forty years of age, it came into his heart to visit his brothers, the children of Israel.
When he saw someone being treated unjustly, he rescued him and avenged the oppressed man by killing the Egyptian.
He thought his brothers would understand that God would give them deliverance through his hands, but they did not understand.
The next day he appeared to them again as they were fighting with each other, and he tried to bring them to peace, saying, “Men, you are brothers. Why are you treating each other unjustly?”
But the man who was treating his neighbor unjustly pushed him away, saying, “Who appointed you ruler and judge over us?
Do you want to kill me as you killed the Egyptian yesterday?”
At these words Moses fled and became a foreign resident in the land of Midian. There he fathered two sons.
When forty years had passed, an angel appeared to him in the wilderness of Mount Sinai, in a flame of fire coming from a bush.
When Moses saw it, he was amazed at the sight. As he approached to look, the voice of the Lord came, saying,
“I am the God of your ancestors, the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.” Moses began trembling and did not dare to look.
The Lord said to him, “Remove the sandal from your foot, for the place where you are standing is holy ground.
I have indeed seen the suffering of my people in Egypt, and I have heard their groaning. And [?] came down to rescue them. Now, then, come, and I will send you to Egypt.”
This is the Moses whom they rejected, saying, “Who appointed you ruler and judge over us?” God sent this man as ruler and deliverer with the help of the angel who appeared to him in the bush.
He was the one who led them out, performing signs and wonders in Egypt, at the Red Sea, and in the wilderness for forty years.
He was the one who said to the children of Israel, “God will raise up a prophet for you from among your brothers, like me.”
He was the one who was in the assembly in the wilderness, with the one who spoke to him on Mount Sinai and with our ancestors. He was the one who received living words to give to you.
Our ancestors refused to obey him. Instead, they rejected him and turned back to Egypt in their hearts.
They said to Aaron, “Make gods for us to lead us. For this Moses, who brought us out of the land of Egypt—we do not know what has happened to him.”
They made the calf in those days, offered a sacrifice to the idol, and rejoiced in the works of their hands.

But God turned them over to worship the army of heaven, as it is written in the book of the prophets: “Did you offer slaughtered animals and sacrifices to me for forty years in the wilderness, house of Israel?”
“You took up the tent of Moloch and the star of the god Rephan, the images you made to worship. And I will deport you beyond Babylon.”
Our ancestors had the tent of testimony with them in the wilderness, just as the one who spoke to Moses had commanded him to make it according to the pattern he had seen.
Our ancestors who came after the earlier generations brought this in with Joshua when they took possession of the nations that God drove out before our ancestors, until the days of David.
He found favor before God and asked to find a dwelling place for the God of Jacob.
But Solomon built him a house.
Yet the Most High does not live in things made by human hands, as the prophet says,
“Heaven is my throne, and the earth is the footstool for my feet. What kind of house will you build for me, says the Lord, or what is my place of rest?
Did not my hand make all these things?”
You stubborn people, uncircumcised in heart and ears! You always resist the Holy Spirit. You are just like your ancestors.
Which of the prophets did your ancestors not persecute? They killed those who announced that the Righteous One was coming. You have now become his betrayers and murderers.
You received the law through the decrees of angels, but you did not keep it.
When they heard these things, they were furious in their hearts and gnashed their teeth at him.
But he, filled with the Holy Spirit, looked up to heaven and saw the glory of God and Jesus standing at God's right hand.
He said, “Look! I see the heavens open and the Son of Man standing at God's right hand.”
When the people heard these things, they shouted loudly, covered their ears with their hands, and rushed at him all together.
They threw him out of the city and stoned him. The witnesses laid their clothes at the feet of a young man named Saul.

They stoned Stephen as he called out, saying, “Lord Jesus, receive my spirit.” Acts 7:60. Then he knelt down and shouted loudly, “Lord, do not hold this sin against them.” When he had said this, he fell asleep.

Saul approved of his killing. On that day, distress and great persecution came upon the church in Jerusalem. Everyone scattered throughout the regions of Judea and Samaria, except for the apostles alone, who remained in Jerusalem.
Devout men buried Stephen and mourned deeply over him.
Saul was ravaging the church, entering houses, dragging out men and women, and throwing them into prison.
Those who had scattered went from city to city, proclaiming the word.
Philip went down to a city in Samaria and proclaimed Christ to them.
The crowds all paid close attention to what Philip said as they listened to him and saw the signs he performed.
For unclean spirits came out of many who were possessed by them, crying out loudly. He also healed many who were paralyzed or lame.
There was great joy in that city.
There was a man in the city named Simon who practiced magic and amazed the people of Samaria, saying of himself, “I am he.”
They all paid attention to him, from the least to the greatest, saying, “This man is the great power of God.”
They paid attention to him because he had amazed them with his magic for a long time.
But when they heard Philip proclaiming the good news of the kingdom of God and the name of Jesus Christ, both men and women were baptized.
Simon himself also believed. After he was baptized, he stayed close to Philip. When he saw the signs and great miracles Philip performed, he was amazed.
When the apostles in Jerusalem heard that Samaria had accepted the word of God, they sent Peter and John to them.
When these men arrived, they prayed for them so that they might receive the Holy Spirit.
For he had not yet come down upon any of them; they had only been baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus.
Then they laid their hands on them, and they received the Holy Spirit.
When Simon saw that the Spirit was given through the laying on of the apostles' hands, he brought them money,
saying, “Give me this authority too, so that anyone on whom I lay my hands may receive the Holy Spirit.”
But Peter said to him, “May your money perish with you, because you thought that God's gift could be bought with money.”
You have no part or share in this matter, for your heart is not right before God.
So repent of your wickedness and plead with the Lord, so that perhaps the thought of your heart may be forgiven you.
For I see that you are in bitter gall and bound by injustice.
Simon answered, saying, “You yourselves plead with the Lord for me, so that none of the things you have said may come upon me.”
Then, after they had testified to the crowd and spoken the word of the Lord to them, they returned to Jerusalem. As they traveled, they proclaimed the good news to many Samaritan villages.
The angel of the Lord spoke to Philip, saying, “Get up and travel at noon along the deserted road that goes down from Jerusalem to Gaza.”
He got up and went. And there was an Ethiopian man, a eunuch and an official of Candace, queen of the Ethiopians, who was in charge of all her wealth. He had come to Jerusalem to worship.
As he was returning, he was sitting in his chariot, reading Isaiah the prophet.
The Spirit said to Philip, “Go over and stay close to this chariot.”
Philip ran over and heard him reading Isaiah the prophet. He said to the eunuch, “Do you understand what you are reading?”
He said to him, “How can I, unless someone explains it to me?” And he asked Philip to climb up and sit beside him.

The passage of Scripture he was reading was this: “Like a sheep, he was brought to the place of his slaughter, and like a lamb before the one who shears it, he makes no sound. In the same way, he did not open his mouth.
In his humiliation, justice was taken away from him. Who can describe his generation? For his life will be taken away from the earth.”
The eunuch responded and said to Philip, “Please tell me: about whom is the prophet saying this—himself or someone else?”
Philip opened his mouth and, beginning with this Scripture, proclaimed to him the good news of the Lord Jesus Christ.
As they traveled along the road, they came to some water. The eunuch said to Philip, “Here is water. What prevents me from being baptized?”
Philip ordered the chariot to stop. They both went down into the water, and Philip baptized him.
When they came up out of the water, a spirit of the Lord snatched Philip away, and the eunuch did not see him again, for he continued on his way rejoicing.
Philip was found in Azotus, and as he traveled he preached in all the towns until he came to Caesarea.
Saul, still filled with threats and murder against the Lord’s disciples, went to the high priest.
He asked him for letters to the synagogues in Damascus, so that if he found anyone belonging to the Way, whether men or women, he could bring them bound to Jerusalem.
As he traveled and drew near Damascus, suddenly a light from heaven shone upon him.
When he fell to the ground, he heard a voice saying to him, “Saul, Saul, why are you persecuting me?”
He said, “Who are you, Lord?” The Lord said, “I am Jesus, whom you are persecuting.
But get up and go into the city, and you will be told what you must do.”
The men traveling with him stood speechless. They heard the voice but did not understand, for they saw no one.
Saul got up from the ground, but although his eyes were open, he could not see. They guided him and brought him into Damascus.
He spent three days unable to see, and he neither ate nor drank.
There was a disciple in Damascus named Ananias. The Lord said to him in a vision, “Ananias!” He replied, “Here I am, Lord.”
The Lord said to him, “Get up and go to the street called Straight. At Judas’s house, ask for a man from Tarsus named Saul, for he is praying.
He has seen a man named Ananias come in and lay his hand on him so that he may see again.”
Ananias answered, “Lord, I have heard from many people about this man and how much harm he has done to your holy people in Jerusalem.”
“And here too he has received authority from the chief priests to arrest everyone who calls on your name.”
The Lord said to him, “Go, for this man is my chosen instrument to carry my name before the nations, kings, and the children of Israel.
For I will show him the sufferings he will undergo for my name.”

Ananias went and entered the house. He laid his hands on Saul and said, “Saul, my brother, the Lord Jesus has sent me—the one who appeared to you on the road you were traveling—so that you may see again and be filled with the Holy Spirit.”
Immediately, things like scales fell from his eyes, and he could see again. Immediately he got up and was baptized.
After eating, he regained his strength. He stayed with the disciples in Damascus for several days.
And immediately he proclaimed the Lord Jesus in the Jewish synagogues, saying, “He is the Christ, the Son of God.”

Everyone who heard him was astonished and said, “Is this not the man who destroyed those in Jerusalem who call on this name? And was he not sent here for this very purpose, to bring them bound before the chief priests?”
Saul grew stronger and stronger and confounded the Jews living in Damascus by showing them that this man is the Christ.
After many days had passed, the Jews plotted to kill him.
Saul was told about their plot. They were watching the gates day and night so that they could kill him.
But the disciples took him at night and lowered him in a basket through the wall.
When he went up to Jerusalem, he tried to join the disciples, but they were all afraid of him and did not believe that he was a disciple.

But Barnabas took him and brought him before the apostles. He told them how Saul had seen the Lord on the road, that the Lord had spoken with him, and how he had spoken boldly in Damascus in the name of Jesus.
He stayed with them, going in and out in Jerusalem and speaking boldly in the name of the Lord.
He spoke and argued with the Greeks, but they set about trying to kill him.
When the brothers learned of this, they brought him down to Caesarea that night and sent him to Tarsus.
The church throughout Judea, Galilee, and Samaria was at peace and was being built up. It lived in reverence for the Lord and grew through the encouragement of the Holy Spirit.
As Peter traveled among them all, he also went to the holy ones living in Lydda.
There he found a man named Aeneas, who had been paralyzed and lying on a bed for eight years.
Peter looked at him and said, “Aeneas, the Lord Jesus Christ has healed you. Get up and make your bed.” And immediately he got up.
Everyone living in Lydda and Sharon saw him, and many turned to God.
There was a sister in Joppa named Tabitha, whose name is translated as Dorcas. She was full of every kind of good deed and acts of charity, which she regularly did.
In those days she became sick and died. They washed her and laid her in an upstairs room.
Lydda was near Joppa. When they heard that Peter was there, they sent two men to him, pleading with him and saying, “Do not delay in coming to us.”

Peter got up and went with them. When he arrived, they took him upstairs to the upper room. All the widows stood beside him, weeping and showing him the tunics and clothes that Dorcas used to make while she was with them.

Peter sent everyone outside, knelt down, and prayed. Then he turned toward the body and said, “Tabitha, get up in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ.” She immediately opened her eyes, and when she saw Peter, she sat up.
He gave her his hand and helped her stand up. Then he called the holy people and the widows and presented her to them alive.
This became known throughout Joppa, and many believed in the Lord.
He stayed in Joppa for many days with a man named Simon, a tanner.
There was a man in Caesarea named Cornelius, a centurion in the military unit called the Italian Cohort.
He was devout and feared God, along with his whole household. He gave generously to the people in need and prayed to the Lord at all times.
At about the ninth hour of the day, he clearly saw in a vision an angel of God come in to him and say to him, “Cornelius!”
He stared at him in fear and said, “What is it, Lord?” The angel said to him, “Your prayers and your gifts to those in need have gone up before God as a reminder of you.
Now send men to Joppa and send for Simon, who is called Peter.
He is staying with a man named Simon, a tanner, whose house is beside the sea.”
When the angel who had spoken with him left, he called two of his servants and a devout soldier from among those who regularly attended him.
He told them everything and sent them to Joppa.
The next day, while they were traveling and approaching the city, Peter went up onto the roof to pray at about the sixth hour.
He became hungry and wanted to eat. While they were preparing food for him, he fell into a trance.
He saw heaven open and something like a large sheet, tied at its four corners, being lowered to the earth.
Inside it were all kinds of animals, the reptiles of the earth, and the birds of the sky.
A voice came to him: “Get up, Peter. Kill and eat.”
Peter said, “Certainly not, Lord! I have never eaten anything defiled or unclean.”
The voice came to him again a second time, saying, “Do not treat as defiled what God has made clean.”
This happened three times, and the sheet was taken back up into heaven.
Peter was inwardly puzzled about what the vision he had seen meant. Just then, the men sent by Cornelius had asked for Simon’s house and arrived at the gate.
They called out and asked, “Is Simon, who is called Peter, staying here?”
While Peter was thinking about the vision, the Spirit said to him, “Look, three men are looking for you.”
But get up, go downstairs, and go with them without hesitation, because I am the one who sent them.
Peter went downstairs and said to the men, “Here I am, the one you are looking for. What is the reason you have come?”

They said to him, “Cornelius, a centurion, is a righteous man who fears God and is well spoken of by the whole Jewish nation. A holy angel instructed him to send for you to come to his house and to hear what you have to say.”
So Peter invited them in and gave them lodging. The next day he got up and left with them, and some of the brothers from Joppa went with him.
The next day he went to Caesarea. Cornelius was waiting for them, having called together his relatives and close friends.
When Peter entered, Cornelius met him, fell at his feet, and worshiped him.
But Peter lifted him up, saying, “Stand up. I too am a human being.”
As he talked with him, he went inside and found a large crowd gathered.
He said to them, “You know that it is unlawful for a Jewish person to associate with or visit someone of another nation. But God has shown me not to call any person defiled or unclean.
That is why, when you sent for me, I came without objection. So I ask you: why did you send for me?”
Cornelius said, “Four days ago, up to this very hour, I was fasting, and I was praying in my house at the ninth hour. Suddenly a man stood before me in bright clothing,
saying, ‘Cornelius, your prayer has been heard, and your acts of charity have been remembered before God.
So send to Joppa and summon Simon, who is called Peter. He is staying in the house of Simon the tanner, by the sea. He will come and tell you words through which you will be saved.’
I sent for you immediately, and you did well to come. Now we are all here before you to hear what God has commanded you to say.”
Then Peter began to speak and said, “I truly understand that God does not show favoritism,
but in every nation, anyone who fears him and does what is right is accepted by him.
For he sent his message to the people of Israel, proclaiming the good news of peace through Jesus Christ, who is Lord of everyone.
You know what happened throughout Judea, beginning in Galilee after the baptism that John proclaimed:
Jesus of Nazareth—how God anointed him with the Holy Spirit and power. He went among them doing good and healing everyone oppressed by the devil, because God was with him.
We are witnesses of everything he did in the region of Judea and in Jerusalem. They killed him by hanging him on a tree.
God raised him on the third day and allowed him to appear,
not to all the people, but to those whom God had chosen beforehand as witnesses—to us, who ate and drank with him for forty days after he rose from the dead.
He commanded us to preach to the people and to testify that he is the one appointed by God as judge of the living and the dead.
All the prophets testify about him that everyone who believes in him receives forgiveness of their sins through his name.”
While Peter was still saying these words, the Holy Spirit fell upon everyone listening to the message.
The circumcised believers who had come with Peter were amazed that the gift of the Holy Spirit had been poured out on the other nations too.
For they heard them speaking in other languages and giving glory to God. Then Peter replied,
“Can anyone withhold the water and prevent these people from being baptized, since they too have received the Holy Spirit just as we have?”
He ordered them to be baptized in the name of Jesus Christ, and he stayed with them for several days.
The apostles and the brothers who were in Judea heard that the Gentiles had accepted the word of God.
When Peter went up to Jerusalem, the circumcised brothers argued with him,
saying, “You went into the homes of uncircumcised men and ate with them.”
Peter began explaining the matter to them from the beginning, saying,
“I was praying in the city called Joppa, and in a trance I saw a vision: an object like a large sheet being lowered from heaven by its four corners. It came down to me.”
“I looked and examined it closely. I saw the animals of the earth, wild beasts, reptiles, and birds of the sky.
I also heard a voice saying to me, ‘Get up, Peter. Slaughter and eat.’
And I said, ‘No, Lord! Nothing defiled or unclean has ever entered my mouth.’
The voice answered from heaven a second time, ‘Do not call defiled what God has made clean.’
This happened three times, and everything was taken up into heaven.
And immediately, three men arrived at the house where I was, having been sent to me from Caesarea.
The Spirit said to me, ‘Go with them without any hesitation.’ These six brothers also came with me, and we entered the man’s house.
He told us how he had seen the angel standing in his house and saying to him, ‘Send to Joppa and summon Simon, who is called Peter.
He will speak words to you through which you and your entire household will be saved.’
When I began to speak, the Holy Spirit fell on them just as on us at the beginning.
Then I remembered the Lord’s words, how he said, ‘John baptized with water, but you will be baptized with the Holy Spirit.’
So if God gave them the same gift that he gave us, since they believed in the Lord Jesus Christ, who was I to be able to stand in God’s way?”
When they heard these things, they became silent and gave glory to God, saying, “Then God has also granted the Gentiles repentance so that they may live.”
Those who had been scattered by the persecution that arose over Stephen traveled as far as Phoenicia, Cyprus, and Antioch, speaking the word to no one except Jews.
But some of them were men from Cyprus and Cyrene. When they came to Antioch, they also spoke to the Greeks [?], proclaiming the Lord Jesus.
The Lord’s hand was with them, and a great number believed and turned to the Lord.
News about them reached the ears of the church in Jerusalem, and they sent Barnabas to go to Antioch.
When he arrived and saw the grace of God, he rejoiced and urged everyone to remain faithful to the Lord.
For he was a good man, full of the Holy Spirit and faith, and a large crowd joined the Lord.
Then he went to Tarsus to look for Saul.
When he found him, he brought him to Antioch. They spent a year there gathering in the church and teaching a large crowd. It was in Antioch that the disciples were first called Christians.
In those days, some prophets came from Jerusalem to Antioch.
One of them, named Agabus, stood up and indicated through the Spirit that a great famine would come upon the whole inhabited world. This happened during the reign of Claudius.
The disciples decided that each of them would contribute according to what they had, and send relief to the brothers living in Judea.
They did this, sending it to the elders through Barnabas and Saul.
At that time, King Agrippa set about mistreating some members of the church.
He killed James, John's brother, with a sword.
When he saw that this pleased the Jews, he went on to arrest Peter as well. These were the days of Unleavened Bread.
After arresting him, he put him in prison and handed him over to sixteen soldiers to guard him. He intended to bring him out before the people after Passover.
So Peter was kept securely guarded in prison, while the church prayed earnestly to God for him.
On the night when Agrippa was about to bring him out, Peter was sleeping between two soldiers, bound with two chains, while guards at the door watched over the prison.
Suddenly an angel of the Lord stood beside Peter, and a light shone in the room. He struck Peter's side and woke him, saying, "Get up quickly!" And the chains fell off his hands.
The angel said to him, "Fasten your belt and put your sandals on your feet." He did so. Then he said to him, "Put on your robe and follow me."
He went out and followed him, not knowing that what the angel was doing was real, for he thought he was seeing a vision.

After they had gone out through the first door and the second, they came to the iron gate that opened onto the city. It opened for them by itself. They went out and reached the first street, and immediately the angel left him.
When Peter came to his senses, he said, "Now I truly understand that the Lord sent his angel and rescued me from Agrippa's hand and from everything the Jewish people were expecting."
When he realized this, he went to the house of Mary, the mother of John who was called Mark, where many people were gathered and praying.
When he knocked at the entrance gate, a young girl named Rhoda came out to answer.
When she recognized Peter's voice, she was so joyful that she did not open the gate. Instead, she ran inside and told them that Peter was standing at the gate.
They said to her, "You are out of your mind!" But she insisted that it was so. They said to her, "It is his angel."
Peter kept knocking. When they opened the gate, they saw him and were astonished.

He motioned to them with his hand to be quiet and told them how the Lord had brought him out of prison. He said, "Tell James and the brothers about these things." Then he went out and left for a deserted place.
When morning came, there was great turmoil among the soldiers over what could have happened to Peter.
When Agrippa searched for him and did not find him, he questioned the guards and ordered them to be taken away and executed. Then he went down from Judea to Caesarea and stayed there.

He was angry with the people of Tyre and Sidon. They came to him together, and after persuading Blastus, who was in charge of the king’s bedroom, they asked for peace, because their country depended on the king’s country for food.
On an appointed day, Herod put on his royal clothing, sat on the judgment seat, and passed judgment on them.
The crowd shouted, “This is the voice of a god, not the voice of a human being!”
Immediately an angel of the Lord struck him because he had not given glory to God. He was eaten by worms and died.
But the word of God grew and spread.
Barnabas and Saul returned from Jerusalem to Antioch after completing their service, taking John, who was called Mark, with them.
There were prophets and teachers in the church at Antioch: Barnabas, Simeon who was called Niger, Lucius of Cyrene, Manaen, the foster brother of Herod the tetrarch, and Saul.
While they were serving the Lord and fasting, the Holy Spirit said to them, “Set Barnabas and Saul apart for me for the work to which I have called them.”
Then they fasted and prayed, laid their hands on them, and sent them off.
After being sent out by the holy ones, they went down to Seleucia, and from there they sailed to Cyprus.
When they arrived in Salamis, they proclaimed the word of God in the Jewish synagogues. They also had John with them as their helper.
After traveling through the whole island as far as Paphos, they found a Jewish man who was a magician and a false prophet, named Bar-Jesus.
He was with the proconsul Sergius Paulus, an intelligent man. The proconsul summoned Barnabas and Saul and wanted to hear the word of God.
But Elymas the magician—for that is how his name is translated—opposed them, trying to turn the proconsul away from the faith.
But Saul, who was also Paul, was filled with the Holy Spirit and looked straight at him.
He said, “You who are full of every kind of deceit and every kind of evil, son of the devil, enemy of all righteousness! Will you not stop twisting the Lord’s straight paths?”

“Now look! The hand of the Lord will be upon you, and you will be blind, unable to see the sun for a time.” Immediately a haze and darkness fell over him, and he went around looking for people to guide him.
Then, when the proconsul saw what had happened, he believed, amazed at the teaching of the Lord.
Paul and his companions sailed from Paphos and came to Perga in Pamphylia. But John left them and returned to Jerusalem.
They left Perga and came to Antioch in Pisidia. On the Sabbath day they entered the synagogue and sat down.
After the reading of the Law and the Prophets, the synagogue leaders sent word to them, saying, “Brothers, if you have a word of encouragement, speak it before the people.”
Paul stood up and motioned to them with his hand, saying, “Men of Israel and you who fear God, listen!
The God of Israel chose our ancestors and made the people great during their stay as foreigners in the land of Egypt. With an uplifted arm he brought them out of that place.
He cared for them for forty years in the wilderness.
He destroyed seven nations in the land of Canaan and gave them their land as an inheritance,
for four hundred and fifty years. And he gave them judges until Samuel the prophet.
Afterward they asked for a king, and God gave them Saul son of Kish, a man from the tribe of Benjamin, for forty years.
After removing him, he raised up David as their king. He testified about him, saying, ‘I have found David son of Jesse, a man after my own heart, who will do everything I want.’
From his descendants, then, in accordance with a promise, God raised up Jesus as a Savior for Israel.
Before his arrival, John had proclaimed a baptism of repentance to all the people.
As John was finishing his course, he said before the crowd, “Why do you think that I am he? I am not he. But look, someone is coming after me whose sandals I am not worthy to untie.”
“Brothers, descendants of Abraham, and those among you who fear God, the message of this salvation has been sent to us.
For those who live in Jerusalem and their rulers did not recognize him or the words of the prophets that are read every Sabbath. They condemned them and fulfilled them.
Although they found no grounds for a death sentence against him, they asked Pilate to put him to death.
When they had fulfilled everything written about him, they took him down from the tree and laid him in a tomb.
But God raised him from the dead.
For many days he appeared to those who had gone with him from Galilee up to Jerusalem. They are now his witnesses before the people.
And we too bring you the good news of the promise made to our ancestors,
that God has fulfilled it for their children by raising up the Lord Jesus Christ for us, as it is written in the second psalm: ‘You are my Son; today I have fathered you.’
As for his raising him from the dead, never to return to decay, he said this: ‘I will give you the holy and sure blessings of David.’
For he also says in another place, ‘You will not allow your Holy One to experience decay.’
For David served God's purpose in his own generation, fell asleep, was laid beside his ancestors, and experienced decay.
But the one whom God raised did not experience decay.
Therefore, my brothers, let it be known to you that through Jesus the forgiveness of your sins is proclaimed to you, and everything from which you could not be justified by the law of Moses.
Everyone who believes in him will be made righteous.
So be careful not to let what was spoken through the prophet come upon you:
‘Look, you scoffers! Be amazed and perish, because I will do a work in your days, a work you will not believe even if someone tells you about it.’”
As they were going out, the people begged him to speak these words to them on the following Sabbath.
When the synagogue meeting broke up, many Jews and devout converts followed Paul and Barnabas. They spoke with them and urged them to remain in the grace of God.
On the following Sabbath, almost the whole city gathered to hear the word of the Lord.
When the Jews saw the crowd, they were filled with jealousy and contradicted what Paul was saying, speaking abusively.

Paul and Barnabas spoke boldly and said to them, “It was necessary to speak the word of God to you first. Since you reject it and do not judge yourselves worthy of life, look, we will turn to the Gentiles.
For this is what Scripture has said: ‘I have made you a light for the Gentiles, so that you may bring salvation to the ends of the earth.’”
When the Gentiles heard this, they rejoiced and glorified the word of the Lord, and those who had been appointed to eternal life believed.
The word of the Lord spread throughout the whole region.
But the Jews stirred up the wealthy women who worshiped God and the leading men of the city. They started a persecution against Paul and Barnabas and drove them out of their territory.
But they shook the dust off their feet against them and went to Iconium.
The disciples were filled with joy and the Holy Spirit.
Once again, as was their custom, they entered the synagogue of the Jews and spoke in such a way that a great number of both Jews and Greeks believed.
But the Jews who did not believe rose up and embittered the minds of the Gentiles against the brothers.
They stayed there a long time, speaking boldly in reliance on the Lord, who bore witness to the message of his grace by granting that signs and wonders be done through their hands.
The people of the city were divided: some sided with the Jews, and others with the apostles.
When the Gentiles and the Jews, together with their rulers, made an attempt to mistreat them and stone them,
They learned about it and fled to the cities of Lycaonia, Lystra and Derbe, and the surrounding region.
And they preached the good news there.
There was a man sitting in Lystra whose feet were weak. He had been lame from his mother's womb and had never walked.
He was listening to Paul speak. Paul looked intently at him and realized that he had faith to be healed.
He said to him in a loud voice, “I tell you in the name of Jesus Christ: get up and stand on your feet!” And he jumped up and walked.
When the crowds saw what Paul had done, they raised their voices in their own language, saying, “The gods have taken the likeness of human beings and have come down to us!”
They called Barnabas Zeus and Paul Hermes, because he was the one who was powerful in speaking.
The priest of Zeus, who was outside the city, brought bulls and wreaths to the gates. Together with the crowds, he wanted to offer a sacrifice.
When the apostles Barnabas and Paul heard this, they tore their clothes and rushed out into the crowd, shouting

and saying, “Men, what are these things you are doing? We too are human beings. We are proclaiming the good news to you so that you will leave these worthless things and turn to the living God, who made heaven, earth, the sea, and everything in them.
In past generations, he allowed all the nations to go their own ways.
Yet he did not leave himself without a witness to them: he did good to them, giving rain from heaven and fruitful seasons, satisfying their hearts with food and joy.”
Even by saying these things, they barely managed to keep the crowds from offering sacrifice to them.
Some Jews came from Antioch and Iconium, persuaded the crowds, stoned Paul, and dragged him outside the city, thinking he was dead.
But when the disciples gathered around him, and evening came, he got up and went into the city. The next day he left with Barnabas for Derbe.
After they had proclaimed the good news in that city and taught many people, they returned to Lystra, Iconium, and Antioch.
They strengthened the souls of the disciples, urging them to remain in the faith and saying, “We will enter the kingdom of God through many hardships.”
They appointed elders for them in each church, prayed with fasting, and entrusted them to the Lord in whom they had believed.
And after they had traveled through Pisidia, they came to Perga in Pamphylia.
And after they had spoken the word in that place, they went to Attalia.
From there they sailed to Antioch, the place where they had been entrusted to God's grace for the work they had completed.
When they arrived, they gathered the church and told them everything God had done with them, and how he had opened a door of faith to the Gentiles.
They stayed there a long time with the disciples.
Some people came from Judea and taught the brothers, saying, "Unless you are circumcised and follow the practice of Moses, you cannot be saved."

When a dispute and a great debate arose between Paul and Barnabas and these people, they appointed Paul and Barnabas and some other brothers from among them to go to the apostles and elders in Jerusalem about this question.
So, after the church sent them on their way, they passed through Phoenicia and Samaria, telling of the conversion of the Gentiles and bringing great joy to all the brothers.
When they went up to Jerusalem, the church, the apostles, and the elders welcomed them warmly. They told them what God had done with them among the Gentiles.
But some believers from the party of the Pharisees stood up and said, "They must be circumcised and instructed to keep the law of Moses."
The apostles and elders gathered to consider this matter.
After much debate, Peter stood up and said to them, "My brothers, you know that from the early days God chose that the Gentiles should hear the message of the good news through my mouth and believe.
And God, who knows people's hearts, testified on their behalf by giving them the Holy Spirit, just as he gave him to us.
He made no distinction between us and them, cleansing their hearts through faith.
So now, why are you testing God by placing a yoke on the necks of the disciples that neither our ancestors nor we have been able to bear?
Instead, we believe that we are saved through the grace of our Lord Jesus, just as they are."
The whole crowd fell silent and listened to Barnabas and Paul as they described the signs and wonders God had done among the Gentiles through them.
After they fell silent, James responded, saying, "Brothers, listen to me.
Simeon has told us how God first visited the Gentiles to take from among them a people for his name.
The words of the prophets agree with this, as it is written:
'After these things I will return and rebuild David's tent, which has fallen. I will rebuild its ruins and set it upright,
so that the rest of humanity may seek the Lord, along with all the Gentiles over whom my name has been invoked, says the Lord,
who has made these things known from eternity.'
Therefore, my judgment is that we should not trouble those among the Gentiles who are turning to God.
Instead, we should write to them to abstain from the defilements of idols, sexual immorality, a dead animal, and blood, and not to do what they do not want to happen to them.
For from ancient generations Moses has had people proclaiming him in every city, with his writings being read in the synagogues every Sabbath."

Then the apostles and the elders, together with the whole church, decided to choose men from among themselves and send them to Antioch with Paul and Barnabas: Judas, who was called Barnabas, and Silas, leading men among the brothers.
They sent through them a letter written as follows: The apostles and elders write to the brothers in Antioch, Syria, and Cilicia who are Gentiles: Greetings.
Since we have heard that some people from among us came to you and troubled you with their words, distressing your souls, although we gave them no instructions,
we decided, having gathered together, to choose men and send them to you with our beloved Barnabas and Paul,
men who have given their lives for the name of our Lord Jesus.
So we have sent Judas and Silas, who will also tell you these same things in person.
For the Holy Spirit and we decided not to place any burden on you beyond these necessary requirements:

Abstain from food sacrificed to idols, blood, dead animals, and sexual immorality. And do not do the things you do not want to happen to you. If you keep yourselves from these things, you will do well. Farewell.
So, after they were sent off, they went down to Antioch, gathered the community together, and gave them the letter.
When they read it, they rejoiced at its encouragement.
Judas and Silas, who were themselves prophets, encouraged and strengthened the brothers with many words.
After they had spent some time there, the brothers sent them off in peace to Jerusalem, to those who had sent them.
But Silas decided to remain there.
Paul and Barnabas stayed in Antioch, teaching and proclaiming the good news of God's word along with many others.
After some days, Paul said to Barnabas, “Let us return and visit the brothers in every city where we proclaimed the word of the Lord, to see how they are doing.”
Barnabas wanted to take John, who was called Mark, with him.
But Paul thought they should not take the man who had left them in Pamphylia and had not gone with them to the work.
A sharp disagreement arose, so that they separated from each other. Barnabas took Mark and sailed to Cyprus.
But Paul chose Silas and departed, having been entrusted by the brothers to the grace of the Lord.
He traveled through Syria and Cilicia, strengthening the churches.
He also arrived at Derbe and Lystra. There was a disciple there named Timothy, the son of a believing Jewish woman, but his father was Greek.
The brothers in Lystra and Iconium spoke well of him.
Paul wanted him to travel with him, so he took him and circumcised him because of the Jews who lived in that area, for they all knew that his father was Greek.
As they traveled through the cities, they handed over to the people the decisions made by the apostles and elders in Jerusalem, for them to observe.
So the churches were strengthened in the faith and increased in number every day.
They traveled through Phrygia and the region of Galatia, having been prevented by the Holy Spirit from speaking the word in Asia.
When they came to Mysia, they tried to enter Bithynia, but the Spirit did not allow them.
Passing by Mysia, they went down to Troas.
A vision appeared to Paul during the night, as though a man from Macedonia were standing before him, pleading with him and saying, “Come to Macedonia and help us.”
When he got up, he told us about the vision. Immediately we sought to leave for Macedonia, telling them that the Lord had called us to preach to them.
We sailed from Troas and went straight to Samothrace, and the next day to Neapolis.
From there we went to Philippi, a city that is a colony and the leading city of that district of Macedonia. We stayed in this city for some days.
On the Sabbath day, we went outside the gate to the river, to a place where we used to pray. We sat down and spoke with the women who had come out to us.
A woman named Lydia was listening. She was a seller of purple cloth from the city of Thyatira and worshiped God. The Lord opened her heart to pay attention to what Paul was saying.
When she and her household were baptized, she pleaded with us, saying, “If you have judged me to be faithful to the Lord, come and stay in my house.” And she persuaded us.
As we were going to pray, a young girl possessed by a spirit of divination met us. She brought her masters a great deal of money by telling fortunes.
She followed Paul and us, shouting, “These men are servants of the Most High God, and they proclaim to us the way of salvation.”
She kept doing this for many days. When Paul became annoyed, he turned and said to the spirit, “I command you in the name of Jesus Christ to come out of her.” And it came out of her that very moment.
When her masters saw that their hope of profit was gone, they seized Paul and Silas and dragged them into the marketplace before the authorities.
They brought them before the magistrates, saying, “These men are Jews, and they are disturbing this city.
They proclaim customs that we, as Romans, are not allowed to accept or practice.”
The crowd rushed against them, and the magistrates tore off their clothes and ordered them to be beaten with rods.
After giving them many blows, they threw them into prison and ordered the jailer to guard them securely.
Having received this order, he threw them into the inner prison and secured their feet in the stocks.
At midnight, Paul and Silas were praying and praising God, and the prisoners were listening to them.
Suddenly there was a great earthquake, so that the foundations of the prison shook. Immediately all the doors opened, and everyone's bonds came loose.
The jailer woke up, and when he saw the prison doors open, he drew his sword and was about to kill himself, thinking that the prisoners had escaped.
But Paul called to him in a loud voice, saying, “Do not harm yourself! We are all here.”
He took a torch, rushed inside, and fell trembling at the feet of Paul and Silas.
He brought them outside and said to them, “Sirs, what must I do to be saved?”
They said, “Believe in the Lord Jesus Christ, and you will be saved, you and your household.”
They spoke the word of the Lord to him and to everyone in his house.
At that hour of the night he took them and washed their wounds, and immediately he and everyone belonging to him were baptized.
He brought them up into his house and set a meal before them. He rejoiced, having believed in the Lord together with his entire household.
When morning came, the magistrates sent officers carrying rods, saying, “Release these men.”
The jailer told Paul these words: “The magistrates have sent orders to release you. So now come out and go in peace.”

But Paul said to them, “They beat us publicly, although we are Roman citizens and had committed no crime, and threw us into prison. Now are they sending us out secretly? No! Let them come themselves and bring us out.”
The guards reported these words to the magistrates, and they were afraid when they heard that they were Roman citizens.
They came and appealed to them, and after bringing them out, they begged them to leave the city.
After coming out of prison, they went to Lydia. When they saw the brothers, they exhorted them and departed.
They passed through Amphipolis and Apollonia and came to Thessalonica, where there was a Jewish synagogue.
As was Paul's custom, he went in to them and spent three Sabbaths discussing the Scriptures with them.
He explained them and showed them concerning the Christ that he had to die and rise from the dead, and said, “This Jesus whom I proclaim to you is the Christ.”
Some of them were persuaded and joined Paul and Silas, as did a great number of worshiping Greeks and many of the wealthy women.

But the Jews became jealous and went and took with them some wicked men who loitered in the marketplace. They gathered a crowd and threw the city into turmoil. They came to the door of Jason's house and searched for them to bring them out before the crowd.
When they did not find them, they dragged Jason and some of the brothers before the rulers, shouting, “These men who have thrown the world into turmoil have come here too,
and Jason has welcomed them. They are all acting against the king's decrees, saying that there is another king, Jesus.”
They stirred up the crowd and the rulers when they heard these things.
After taking security from Jason and the others, they released them.
The brothers immediately sent Paul and Silas away by night to Berea. When they arrived there, they immediately went into the Jewish synagogue.
These people were more discerning than those in Thessalonica. They received the message with great eagerness, examining the Scriptures every day to see whether these things were so.
Many of them therefore believed, as did wealthy Greek women and a large number of men.
But when the Jews from Thessalonica learned that the word of God had also been proclaimed by Paul in Berea, they came there too, stirring up and agitating the crowds.
The brothers immediately sent Paul away to go down to the sea, but Silas and Timothy remained there.
Those escorting Paul brought him as far as Athens. After receiving an instruction from him for Silas and Timothy to come to him quickly, they departed.
While Paul was waiting for them in Athens, his spirit was deeply troubled within him as he saw that the city was full of shrines to idols.
He discussed with the Jews and the worshipers in their synagogue, and every day in the marketplace with those who came to him.

Some Epicurean and Stoic philosophers were debating with him. Some were saying, “What is this babbler saying?” Others said, “He is proclaiming new gods,” because he was preaching the good news about Jesus and the resurrection of the dead.
They took hold of him and brought him to the Areopagus, saying, “We would like to know what this new teaching is that you are speaking about.
For you are bringing new things to our ears, so we want to know what these things mean.”
For all the Athenians and the foreigners among them spent their time doing nothing except talking about or listening to something new.
Paul stood in the middle of the Areopagus and said, “People of Athens, in every respect I see that you are worshippers of gods [?].

For as I was walking around and looking at the things you worship, I found an altar with this inscription: ‘The God who is not known.’ So the one you worship without knowing him is the one I am proclaiming to you.
God, who made the world and everything in it, is the Lord of heaven and earth. He does not live in temples made by human hands.
Nor does he lack anything that would require him to be served by human hands. He himself gives life to everyone and breath in everything.
He made every nation of people from one person, so that they would live over the whole face of the earth. He determined their appointed times and the boundaries of the places where they would live,
so that they would seek God, in the hope that they might feel their way toward him and find him, although he is not far from each one of us.
For in him we exist, and in him we live and move, as some of your own poets have also said, ‘We are his offspring.’
Since we are God's offspring, we should not think that God is like gold or silver or stone carved by human skill and imagination.
God overlooked the times of ignorance, but now he commands people everywhere to repent,
because he has established a day on which he will judge the inhabited world with justice through a man he has appointed. He has given everyone assurance of this by raising him from the dead.”
When they heard about the resurrection of the dead, some mocked him, but others said, “We will hear you about this.”
And this is how Paul left their midst.
But some people believed and joined him, including Dionysius the Areopagite, a woman named Damaris, and others with them.
After these things, he left Athens and went to Corinth.
He found a Jew named Aquila, a native of Pontus, who had recently come from Italy with his wife Priscilla, because Claudius had ordered all the Jews to leave Rome. He went to visit them.
He stayed with them and worked, because his trade was the same as theirs. Their trade was tentmaking.
Every Sabbath he spoke to them in the synagogue, persuading the Jews and the Greeks.
When Silas and Timothy came from Macedonia, Paul was devoting himself to the word, testifying to the Jews that Jesus is the Christ.
When they opposed him and spoke abusively, he shook out his clothes and said, “Your blood is on your own heads! I am innocent. From now on I will go to the Gentiles.”
He moved from that place and went into the house of a brother named Titus, who worshipped God. His house was close to the synagogue.
Crispus, the leader of the synagogue, believed in the Lord along with his whole household. Many of the Corinthians who heard believed and were baptized.
The Lord said to Paul in a vision at night, “Do not be afraid, but speak and do not keep silent.
“For I am with you, and no one will be able to harm you, because I have many people in this city.”
He stayed there for a year and six months, teaching the word of God among them.
While Gallio was proconsul of Achaia, the Jews rose up together against Paul, laid their hands on him, and brought him before the judgment seat.
They said, “This man persuades people to worship God contrary to the law.”
Just as Paul was about to open his mouth, Gallio said to the Jews, “If some injustice or evil deed had occurred, Jews, it would be reasonable for me to put up with you.
But now, if these are disputes about a word or names concerning your law, see to them yourselves. I do not want to judge matters of this kind.”
And he drove them away from the judgment seat.
Then all the Greeks seized Sosthenes, the synagogue leader, and beat him in front of the judgment seat. Gallio paid no attention to them.
Paul stayed with the brothers for many more days. After this, he said goodbye to them and sailed for Syria with Priscilla and Aquila. He shaved his head at Cenchreae, because he had made a vow.
When they reached Ephesus, Paul went into the synagogue on the following Sabbath and spoke with the Jews.
When they begged him to spend more time there, he did not stay.
Instead, he left those who were in that place and said goodbye to them, saying, “I will return to you again if it is God's will.” Then he departed from Ephesus.
He sailed to Caesarea, and after going up and greeting the church, he went down to Antioch.
After spending some time there, he set out and traveled through the region of Galatia and Phrygia, strengthening all the disciples.
A Jew named Apollos came to Ephesus. He was an Alexandrian by birth, an eloquent man with a strong command of the Scriptures.
He had been instructed in the way of the Lord. With a fervent spirit, he spoke and taught accurately about Jesus, though he knew only the baptism of John.
He began to speak boldly in the synagogue. When Aquila and Priscilla heard him, they took him with them and explained the way of God to him accurately.
The brothers encouraged him when he wanted to go to Achaia, and they wrote to the brothers to welcome him. When he arrived there, he greatly helped those who had believed through grace.
For he vigorously refuted the Jews in public, showing them from the Scriptures that Jesus is the Christ.
While Apollos was in Corinth, Paul traveled through the inland regions and came to Ephesus. He found some disciples there.
He said to them, “Did you receive the Holy Spirit when you believed?” They said to him, “We have not even heard that anyone receives the Holy Spirit.”
